title: Infinite Product Measures and Kolmogorov Extension

items.title: Coordinate maps, finite-coordinate cylinders, and the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra
items.strategy: For an arbitrary index set and measurable coordinate spaces, define finite-coordinate projections and inverse-image cylinders. Identify the sigma-algebra they generate with the library's product sigma-algebra, rather than introducing a competing construction.

items.title: Finite-coordinate cylinders form a $\pi$-system
items.strategy: Pull two cylinders to the finite union of their coordinate supports and intersect their measurable bases. This treats overlapping and disjoint supports uniformly.

items.title: Finite-coordinate cylinder sets form an algebra
items.strategy: At the union of all supports, complements and finite unions are inverse images of the corresponding finite-dimensional measurable sets. Keep this cylinder algebra distinct from the smaller rectangle-cylinder pi-system.

items.title: A consistent family of finite-dimensional distributions
items.strategy: For every finite coordinate set give a law on its finite product, compatible under coordinate projections and reorderings; agreement of one-dimensional marginals is explicitly insufficient.

items.title: Consistent finite-dimensional laws define a well-defined finitely additive cylinder law
items.strategy: Assuming the full coordinate product is nonempty, represent competing cylinder presentations and each finite disjoint decomposition on the union of their coordinate supports. Projection consistency gives presentation-independent values and finite additivity without prematurely calling the law a premeasure.

items.title: The countable-product cylinder premeasure is countably additive
items.strategy: Assuming countable and dependent choice, use Kajino's finite-stage section argument for a countable sequence of arbitrary probability spaces: recursively preserve a positive lower bound for all remaining tail sections, obtain continuity at the empty set, then combine it with finite additivity to get a premeasure. No Polish or compactness hypothesis enters this route.

items.title: Assuming countable and dependent choice, countable products of arbitrary probability spaces
items.strategy: Assuming countable and dependent choice, apply Caratheodory extension to the countably additive cylinder premeasure and use the cylinder pi-system for uniqueness. State only the product-marginal theorem over arbitrary measurable spaces; the later arbitrary-index result is genuinely stronger.

items.title: Coordinate random elements of a countable product are independent
items.strategy: Evaluate finite-coordinate rectangles under the product measure and compare with the finite-family definition of independence, recording the prescribed coordinate laws as well.

items.title: Countably many independent copies of a prescribed law exist
items.strategy: Under countable and dependent choice, specialize the countable product to one repeated measurable probability space and take its coordinate maps, proving existence rather than presupposing a rich source probability space.

items.title: Stochastic processes and their finite-dimensional distributions
items.strategy: Define an indexed family of random elements, allowing varying state spaces, and its ordered finite-dimensional laws through finite-coordinate projections. The full compatible family, not only one-dimensional marginals, is the data.

items.title: Process law, modification, and indistinguishability
items.strategy: Separate equality of finite-dimensional laws, fixed-time almost-sure equality for a modification, and one-null-set equality for indistinguishability. Require a measurable diagonal for the fixed-time equality event and never replace it by an unjustified uncountable intersection.

items.title: Standard Borel spaces
items.strategy: Define a standard Borel measurable space as measurably isomorphic to the Borel measurable space of a Polish space; the measurable structure, not a selected topology, is the datum.

items.title: Finite products of standard Borel spaces are standard Borel
items.strategy: Transport finite products through Polish presentations and the finite-product Polish construction, verifying that the transported Borel sigma-algebra is the finite product sigma-algebra.

items.title: Assuming countable choice, Borel probability measures on Polish spaces are inner regular
items.strategy: Assuming countable choice, fix a complete compatible metric and a countable dense set. At each scale use continuity from below on the increasing finite unions of its open balls to choose one finite union with summable complement loss; intersect the corresponding closed-ball enlargements. Their intersection is closed and totally bounded, hence compact, and countable subadditivity gives the required compact approximation. State the Borel measurability and the compact approximation precisely for the extension proof.

items.title: Assuming the Axiom of Choice, Kolmogorov extension for arbitrary families of standard Borel coordinate spaces
items.strategy: Assuming the Axiom of Choice (and hence countable choice), use consistency for a finitely additive cylinder law; enumerate the countable active coordinates, place each cylinder on a nested finite support containing the first active coordinates, approximate its finite-dimensional base from inside by a compact set, and use successive subsequences plus a diagonal limit to obtain continuity at the empty set. Use AC only to fill inactive coordinates, extend by Caratheodory, and prove uniqueness only on the cylinder sigma-algebra by the cylinder pi-system.

items.title: Arbitrary products of standard Borel probability spaces
items.strategy: Use finite products of the prescribed coordinate laws as the consistent finite-dimensional family and invoke Kolmogorov extension. The measure lives on the cylinder/product sigma-algebra, never the full power set.

items.title: The canonical coordinate process realizes consistent finite-dimensional laws
items.strategy: Equip the product space with the extension measure, take its coordinate projections, and read each requested finite-dimensional law from the defining cylinder values.

items.title: Finite-dimensional distributions determine a process law on the cylinder sigma-algebra
items.strategy: Equal finite-dimensional laws agree on the cylinder pi-system. Apply the pi-lambda uniqueness argument only to its generated cylinder sigma-algebra, never an unspecified larger sigma-algebra.

items.title: Assuming countable choice, cylinder-measurable events depend on only countably many coordinates
items.strategy: Assuming countable choice, show that events determined by some countable coordinate set form a sigma-algebra: select supports for a countable family and use the countable-union theorem. Generated-sigma minimality then proves the claim.

items.title: The cylinder sigma-algebra need not be the full path-space power set
items.strategy: Record the measurable-space boundary of the extension theorems, referring to the countable-coordinate lemma and the companion nonmeasurable path-functional counterexample without asserting an unsupported cardinality classification.

items.title: State-space and index-set boundaries of the two extension routes
items.strategy: Contrast the countable arbitrary-measurable product-marginal theorem with arbitrary-index standard-Borel extension, and direct recursive kernel constructions to the planned Markov-kernel page.

title: Infinite Product Measures and Kolmogorov Extension — Examples

items.title: The infinite fair-coin-toss space
items.strategy: Apply the countable product theorem to $\{0,1\}$ with the fair Bernoulli law, calculate a finite cylinder probability, and identify independent coordinate tosses.

items.title: An i.i.d. sequence with a prescribed law
items.strategy: Under countable and dependent choice, repeat the supplied probability space in the countable product theorem and apply the coordinate-independence corollary to verify the common marginal law and finite-family independence on the canonical cylinder probability space.

items.title: Independent but non-identically distributed coordinates
items.strategy: Use a countable product with unequal Bernoulli parameters, check independence, and exhibit coordinates with different one-dimensional laws.

items.title: A canonical random walk from product increments
items.strategy: Take independent $\{-1,1\}$-valued coordinate increments and define partial sums; verify the finite-dimensional increment law while distinguishing process coordinates from increment coordinates.

items.title: An uncountable Bernoulli coordinate process
items.strategy: For an arbitrary uncountable index set, prescribe fair Bernoulli finite-dimensional product laws and apply the standard-Borel extension theorem, explicitly retaining the cylinder sigma-algebra scope.

items.title: A modification need not be indistinguishable
items.strategy: With uniform $U$ on $[0,1]$, compare the zero process with the process that equals one exactly when $U=t$. Fixed-time disagreement is null, but every outcome disagrees at its own time; check the measurable-diagonal convention.

items.title: One-dimensional marginals alone do not specify a joint law
items.strategy: Compare equal fair bits with two independent fair bits. They have equal one-dimensional marginals but different probability of equality, so full finite-dimensional laws are necessary.

items.title: A noncylinder path functional may fail to be measurable
items.strategy: On an uncountable Bernoulli path space, use the paths with uncountably many ones. The countable-coordinate lemma shows that event is not cylinder-measurable, so its indicator is not a random variable for the canonical construction.
